overall: The AG found the Board violated the law by giving an insufficiently detailed executive session topic on its September 26 notice, found no violation on the October 10 notice or posting-time claims, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the September 26 notice's executive session topic (ongoing litigation and non-union contract negotiations) was too vague.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the September 26 meeting notice was not sufficiently detailed because the notice failed to identify the non-union personnel with which it was negotiating and the litigation matter it planned to discuss.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 10 notice's executive session topic (ongoing litigation) was too vague.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not convene in executive session on October 10, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of the executive session topic listed on that notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the meeting notices lacked the date and time the Town Clerk posted them.
allegations.key_passage: Town Manager Gagne provided this office with copies of the notices that were posted and stamped by the Town Clerk. Thus, we find no violation of the Open Meeting law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
